B.depoimento: I have ordered the construction of 1 knight and 2 spearmen in Barcelona to bolster our home forces. Simultaneously, I am marching a detachment of 3 knights, 2 archers, and 1 spearman to capture the neutral village of Tarragona, securing a vital foothold for our kingdom.
B.plano: Capture Tarragona to expand our territory and increase resource production. Build 1 knight and 2 spearmen in Barcelona to reinforce our capital. Next turn, evaluate the map and plan the next expansion towards Girona or other nearby villages.

A.depoimento: We struck at the neutral villages of Santarem and Evora, sending spearmen to the north and knights to the south. In Lisboa, we began training new knights and spearmen to sustain our march.
A.plano: Take Santarem with 4 spearman, Evora with 3 knights. Build 2 knights and 2 spearman in Lisboa to replenish forces. Next turn, explore Coimbra and Faro.

B.depoimento: I have sent my forces to conquer the neutral villages of Girona and Zaragoza, while building a knight in Barcelona to strengthen my army. My kingdom expands!
B.plano: Conquer Girona and Zaragoza to expand territory. Next turn, build more troops in Barcelona and Tarragona, and plan further expansion towards Castellon and beyond. Watch for enemy movements.

A.depoimento: Our spearman advance on Coimbra to expand our territory. The king's army from Lisboa rushes to support the front lines. We build more spearman to replenish our forces. The south holds with Evora's knights standing ready.
A.plano: Attack Coimbra with 3 spearman from Santarem. Send all troops from Lisboa to Santarem for reinforcement. Build 2 spearman in Lisboa. Next turn, evaluate the battle and plan attacks on Badajoz and Faro. Evora's knights remain for now.

B.depoimento: This turn, we launch a coordinated double strike: Girona's army attacks Huesca, while Zaragoza's forces march on Madrid. We build spearman in Barcelona and Tarragona to reinforce our borders and the sending villages after the attacks. Our goal is to secure key hubs, expand our territory, and prepare for the next phase of our campaign.
B.plano: Conquer Huesca and Madrid to expand our territory and secure key hubs. Reinforce Girona and Zaragoza immediately after the attacks to prevent losing them. Build spearman in Barcelona and Tarragona to prepare for further expansion towards Castellon and the south. Watch for enemy movements and neutral village hardening on turn 5.

A.depoimento: Our armies are on the march. The knights from Santarem lead the assault on Badajoz, supported by archers and spearman. Meanwhile, reinforcements march to Coimbra to prepare for the attack on Porto, and from Lisboa, spearman ride to Evora to strengthen our southern hold. In our villages, we work day and night to build more troops.
A.plano: Next turn: after Badajoz battle, send 3 archers from Coimbra to Porto. From Evora send 1 archer and 1 knight to Faro. Keep the rest in their villages. Consider sending the new knight from Lisboa to Coimbra or Santarem for further operations. Rebuild any losses.

B.depoimento: We have consolidated our power in the east. Our spies report that Salamanca is a key gateway to the west. I have ordered the garrison of Madrid to march on Salamanca, hoping to crush the neutral knights and open the road to the enemy's lands. Meanwhile, our eastern villages are working hard to produce more spearman to swell our ranks.
B.plano: Focus on expanding west towards the enemy capital. Conquer Salamanca to open the path to Coimbra and Porto. Build spearman in eastern villages to prepare for further expansion. Watch for enemy movements and neutral village hardening.

A.depoimento: This turn we strike hard at the neutral villages: archers and a knight from Evora take Faro, while Coimbra's archers assault Porto. We reinforce our western border by sending spearmen from Santarem to Badajoz, and a knight from the capital races to Coimbra for the next wave. Our builders work flat out — knights, archers, and spearmen spring up across the realm. Two more villages mean two more sources of iron and wood. The enemy watches from Salamanca, but our shields hold.
A.plano: Next turn: after Faro and Porto fall, send forces from Evora to Sevilha (4 spearmen, defense 10) and from Porto to Vigo (unexplored). Build more spearman and archers at all villages. Send the new knight from Lisboa (built this turn) to Coimbra for the next push. Keep 2+ spearman in Badajoz for defense. Do NOT attack Salamanca yet — it's a trap until we have overwhelming numbers.

B.depoimento: Our armies strike on two fronts this turn! Salamanca's veterans march on Porto, while Tarragona's spearman horde charges Castellon. We are building knights in every village to swell our ranks. The enemy will not know what hit them!
B.plano: We are launching a double attack this turn: Salamanca to Porto and Tarragona to Castellon. We expect to conquer both, bringing our total to 9 villages. We are also building heavily in all villages, especially knights, to prepare for further expansions next turn towards Teruel and other enemy territories. Do not march from Zaragoza yet; wait for the knights to be built.

A.depoimento: King A's forces have marched on Salamanca. The border villages are reinforced with fresh troops. Our campaign for expansion is underway.
A.plano: Sent 2 knights from Badajoz to Salamanca. Sent 1 knight from Evora to Badajoz. Sent 2 spearmen from Coimbra to Porto. Built troops at all villages. Next turn: check Salamanca capture. Send archers from Coimbra to Porto, and from Evora/Coimbra to Badajoz for Sevilha. Prepare attacks on Vigo and Sevilha.

B.depoimento: This turn, we ordered a double strike: Madrid's archer and knight will march to Porto to conquer the enemy village, while Zaragoza's strong force will attack the neutral Pamplona. We also reinforced Castellon with Tarragona's knights and Zaragoza with Huesca's troops to secure our borders. Our builds focus on knights and archers to maintain our military edge.
B.plano: We are launching a double attack this turn: Madrid to Porto and Zaragoza to Pamplona. We expect to conquer both, bringing our total to 10 villages. We are also reinforcing Castellon with Tarragona's knights and Zaragoza with Huesca's troops to prepare for further expansions next turn towards Valencia and other enemy territories. Do not march from Barcelona yet; keep it strong as our capital.

A.depoimento: This turn, we reinforced Porto against the enemy army and launched a counterattack on Salamanca. Our forces are moving to secure the border and expand our territory.
A.plano: Check the battle results at Porto and Salamanca. If Porto held, begin planning attack on Vigo. If Salamanca conquered, send troops to garrison it and prepare for push east. Build troops in all villages to maintain momentum.

B.depoimento: This turn, we consolidated our positions and prepared for expansion. Castellon's army marched to Valencia, while Zaragoza sent reinforcements to Pamplona to secure our northern flank. Madrid reinforced Salamanca, strengthening our western border against King A. We also began building knights and archers across our villages to grow our military might. Our sights are set on securing Valencia and Pamplona to bring our total to 10 villages.
B.plano: We are focusing on conquering the neutral villages of Valencia and Pamplona this turn to increase our village count to 10. Castellon will attack Valencia, while Zaragoza reinforces Pamplona after the initial assault. Madrid will send its spearman to reinforce Salamanca on our western border. Barcelona and Girona will send troops to Castellon and Zaragoza respectively, to prepare for the next wave of expansions towards Burgos and Teruel next turn. We must not attack the enemy capitals or strongholds yet; we need to build up our forces first.

A.depoimento: Three arrows fly at once! My archers counter the spearman at Vigo and Sevilha, while Coimbra's forces finish the job at Salamanca. If all three fall, I'll have 10 villages and be halfway to victory!
A.plano: Vigo and Sevilha fall to archer counter (18 vs 13 each). Salamanca's first wave weakens it, Coimbra's force finishes it. Santarem's knights stage in Badajoz for Toledo next turn. Build spearman everywhere for the push into knight-heavy Toledo.

B.depoimento: This turn, we reinforce our western border by sending archers from Madrid to Salamanca. We strip Valencia of its weak garrison to reinforce Castellon for the upcoming assault on Teruel. King A's army marches on Salamanca, but our reinforcements should hold the line. Meanwhile, we launch a strike on Burgos with knights from Pamplona, and send knights from Tarragona to Madrid to prepare for the assault on Toledo. Our builders work diligently, producing spearmen and knights to fuel the next wave of conquests. The neutral villages will fall, and our empire will grow.
B.plano: We are focusing on conquering the neutral villages to increase our village count to 14. This turn, we reinforce Salamanca with archers from Madrid to defend against the incoming enemy army. We send Valencia's troops to Castellon to prepare for an attack on Teruel. We send knights from Pamplona to attack Burgos, and knights from Tarragona to Madrid to prepare for an attack on Toledo. We build spearmen in Castellon, Zaragoza, Huesca, Barcelona, Tarragona, and Salamanca, and knights in Madrid and Girona, to prepare for future attacks. We must not attack the enemy capitals or strongholds yet; we n

A.depoimento: Sevilha's walls fall as the Faro archers arrive. In the south, Badajoz's vanguard storms Toledo, its spearmen countering the knight garrison. At Vigo, a cleverly balanced small force slips past Burgos's defenses by the spearman-knight counter. My Porto spearmen ride west to reinforce Vigo for the next push. The Coimbra host perishes at Salamanca - that front must wait until I muster enough archers to crack a defense of 20.
A.plano: Sevilha falls to marching archers (~5 losses expected). Badajoz storms Toledo with 5sp/3ar/2kn - spearman counter vs 5 knights. Vigo takes Burgos with 1sp/1ar/1kn (spearman tie-break grants counter vs 2 knights). Porto sends 4 spearmen to Vigo as staging base. Build knights everywhere for fast follow-on forces. Do NOT attack Salamanca yet - need 7+ archers or 21+ spearmen to beat defense 20. Coimbra's host dies at Salamanca; that front waits.

B.depoimento: This turn, we launch our attack on the neutral village of Teruel with a strong spearman-led force from Zaragoza. We reinforce Salamanca with knights from Madrid to repel the incoming enemy army. We also send troops to Valencia, Burgos, and Zaragoza to prepare for the next phase of our campaign. We build spearmen across all our villages to ensure a steady flow of reinforcements.
B.plano: We attack Teruel with Zaragoza's troops to conquer our 12th village. We reinforce Salamanca with Madrid's knights against the incoming enemy army. We send Castellon's troops to Valencia to prepare for Murcia, Pamplona's troops to Burgos, and Huesca's troops to Zaragoza. We build 2 spearmen in all villages to maximize production. We must focus on neutral villages first to reach 14 villages before attacking enemy territory.

A.depoimento: Sevilha and Toledo are mine — the map has shifted in my favor. Madrid falls this turn with barely a fight; the road east opens. Cordoba is next, and Sevilha's reinforced host will storm it tomorrow. I'm racing every knight I can build toward Vigo to crack Burgos, the last wall before the plains. One village at a time.
A.plano: Madrid conquered (3sp/1ar/1kn from Toledo, attack 9 vs defense 5). Sevilha gets 2sp/3kn from Faro for Cordoba attack next turn (3sp/3ar/3kn = 21 vs 13). Vigo gets 1sp/1ar/1kn from Porto; Coimbra stages 3sp/1kn to Porto for follow-on to Vigo. Build knights in 7 villages + 2 spearmen in Vigo. Keep 1sp in Coimbra for defense. Do NOT attack Teruel - enemy army marching there. Burgos needs 19+ attack; build up over 2-3 turns. Salamanca (defense 28) still too strong.

B.depoimento: This turn, I ordered the build of 2 spearmen in every village to bolster our ranks. I sent Valencia's army to claim Murcia, Burgos's knights and archers to take Vigo, and Zaragoza's spearmen to reinforce Madrid. Pamplona's troops bolstered Burgos, and Castellon's spearmen marched to secure Teruel. With these moves, we set the stage for three conquests next turn.
B.plano: Conquer Teruel, Murcia, and Vigo this turn. Reinforce Madrid with Zaragoza's troops, Burgos with Pamplona's troops, and Teruel with Castellon's troops. Build 2 spearmen in all villages. Next turn, attack Porto from Vigo and Toledo from Teruel. Keep Salamanca strong for future attacks on Coimbra and Badajoz.

A.depoimento: I arm every village this turn — eight knights and two archers — and surge reinforcements to the two weakest targets on the map. From Sevilha I will take the neutral Cordoba (def 13) to open the southern road east; from Vigo I will storm Burgos (def 13) to open the north. My earlier march on Madrid is doomed against its def 20 and I abandon it, redirecting Toledo's strength to the real breakthroughs. The road to Barcelona is opening.
A.plano: Next turn attack Cordoba [11] from Sevilha [9] (should hold ~3sp/4ar/5kn; knight-led counters its archers, 25+ vs def 13) and Burgos [14] from Vigo [10] (~6sp/1ar/4kn, 24 vs def 13). If Porto→Vigo troops haven't arrived in time, delay Burgos one turn. The Toledo→Madrid army dies against def 20 — accept the loss, do not repeat. Keep light guards: Coimbra 1sp, Porto 1sp/2kn, Badajoz 2kn against Salamanca. After Cordoba, build there and attack Murcia [15]; after Burgos, build and attack Pamplona [19] or Madrid [12].

B.depoimento: This turn, we launch a double-pronged attack to expand our territory. From Teruel, our forces march on Toledo, while from Salamanca, our knights and archers strike at Coimbra. Simultaneously, we reinforce Madrid with troops from Zaragoza to hold the line against the enemy's counter-offensive, and we send reinforcements to Burgos and Murcia to prepare for the next phase of our campaign. Our villages are working at full capacity, building spearmens to fuel our expansion.
B.plano: Conquer Toledo and Coimbra this turn. Reinforce Madrid with Zaragoza's troops to defend against the incoming enemy army. Send Pamplona's troops to Burgos and Valencia's troops to Murcia to prepare for future attacks on Vigo and Cordoba. Build spearmen in all affordable villages to grow our army. Next turn, consolidate our new territories and plan the next wave of attacks on Vigo and Cordoba.

A.depoimento: This turn, our armies strike on all fronts with unmatched fury. From Santarem we march on Coimbra; from Toledo we charge into Teruel; from Vigo we assault Burgos; and from Sevilha our knights ride to Cordoba. In every village, blacksmiths work without pause to forge new troops. By dawn, our banners will fly over four new lands, and the enemy will reel from the blows.
A.plano: Next turn, assess battle outcomes and move survivors to reinforce captured villages. Begin building in newly taken villages to boost production. Prepare to attack Murcia from Cordoba and Valencia from Teruel if we have sufficient troops. Keep Santarem and Toledo reinforced as staging grounds for further advances.

B.depoimento: King B's armies strike on three fronts! Madrid takes Toledo, Coimbra takes Porto, and Salamanca marches on Badajoz. We build spearman across the empire to swell our ranks. Reinforcements head to Madrid to keep the capital secure. The trap is set at Coimbra; if the enemy attacks, they will be destroyed!
B.plano: We are launching a major offensive this turn to capture Toledo, Porto, and Badajoz. Madrid sends all troops to Toledo, Coimbra sends all to Porto, Salamanca splits troops to Badajoz and Coimbra. We build spearman in all villages to grow our army. Zaragoza and Burgos send reinforcements to Madrid to keep it defended. Next turn, we will have captured Toledo and Porto, and our armies will be marching on Badajoz. We must watch for enemy counter-attacks on Coimbra and Madrid.

A.depoimento: The enemy attacks on three fronts. I have rushed reinforcements to Coimbra, Badajoz, and Toledo. In a bold move, I am sending the Badajoz garrison to strike at Salamanca, hoping to destroy the enemy army and capture the village. Our interior troops are marching to the borders to reinforce our lines.
A.plano: Next turn, assess battle outcomes. If we hold Coimbra, Badajoz, Toledo and take Salamanca, we will have 11 villages. Then build up and attack Porto and Teruel. Keep reinforcing borders with slow troops arriving later. Ensure Cordoba keeps a small garrison for defense.

A.depoimento: We struck at the enemy's weak points! Our armies attacked Porto, Salamanca, and Teruel simultaneously. Meanwhile, we reinforced our borders and built up our forces. The noose tightens around King B.
A.plano: This turn we attack Porto with knights from Coimbra, Salamanca with archers and knights from Badajoz, and Teruel with archers and knights from Toledo. Reinforcements arrive next turn. Next turn, we will push towards Madrid and Burgos, and explore the unexplored territory. Keep an eye on Vigo and Cordoba for defense.

B.depoimento: King B orders simultaneous attacks on the weak enemy villages of Vigo and Cordoba, while reinforcing the vulnerable Salamanca. The interior villages are busy building knights for a mobile reserve, and the borders are building spearmen. The army in Barcelona begins its march toward the front lines.
B.plano: Attack Vigo and Cordoba to expand territory. Reinforce Salamanca from Madrid and Zaragoza to hold the western border. Build spearmen in all border villages for defense, and knights in interior villages for a future offensive. Move troops from Barcelona to Tarragona to begin a long march to the front. Watch for enemy counterattacks on Porto and Murcia after the attacks.

A.depoimento: This turn my three-pronged strike hits hard: Coimbra's archers and knights fall upon Porto, Badajoz's mixed host upon Salamanca, and Toledo's archers upon Teruel. If these blows land, King B's western wall collapses and my armies can surge eastward toward Madrid and the enemy capital. Every village is forging new knights and archers to feed the advance - the war machine is running full tilt.
A.plano: Attack Porto with 4 archers + 3 knights from Coimbra, Salamanca with 5 spearman/5 archer/5 knight from Badajoz, and Teruel with 3 archers + 2 knights from Toledo. Reinforce Coimbra from Santarem, Badajoz from Evora and Faro, Cordoba from Sevilha, and stage Lisboa's archer via Santarem. Build 7 knights and 6 archers across all villages. Keep only 1 spearman in Toledo - reinforce it next turn from Badajoz in case Madrid counterattacks. Defer Murcia until Cordoba is built up. Check Vigo's status once Porto falls.

B.depoimento: King B's armies strike at Cordoba with 9 spearmen, hoping to break the enemy's weak defense there. Meanwhile, reinforcements flow from Burgos and Zaragoza to Madrid, building a spear wall for the assault on Toledo. Vigo sends its last archers and knights to bolster Porto's defenses. The great build-up continues as we prepare for a decisive push.
B.plano: Attack Cordoba with 9 spearmen from Murcia to conquer it. Reinforce Madrid with 10 spearmen from Burgos and 4 from Zaragoza to prepare for an attack on Toledo next turn. Reinforce Porto with 1 archer and 1 knight from Vigo. Build spearmen in all border villages and knights in interior villages to grow the army.
